brief.t: Started in 2000 as a joint venture of ICICI Bank and the UK's Prudential plc; in Sep 2016 it became the first insurance company listed on India's stock exchanges.

Renamed ICICI Life Insurance Ltd on 22 Sep 2026, after Prudential decided to cut its stake from about 22% to below 10% (to buy control of Bharti Life). ICICI Bank owns about 52.8% and is the promoter.

New leader: Anup Bagchi resigned on 13 Oct 2026 to become HDFC Bank's MD & CEO; Sidharatha Mishra, a 26-year ICICI Bank veteran, was appointed MD & CEO from 14 Oct 2026. Sandeep Batra (ICICI Bank ED) is Chairman.
FY 2025-26 profit was ₹1,600 crore (+35%); VNB rose 11% to ₹2,629 crore at a 24.7% margin.
Q2 FY27 (Jul–Sep 2026) profit rose 25% to ₹374 crore; H1 FY27 VNB grew 22% to ₹1,283 crore with margin up to 26%, helped by protection (term) sales up about 40%.

timeline.t: Incorporated in Mumbai (Jul 2000) as ICICI Prudential Life, a JV of ICICI Bank and Prudential; IRDAI registration in Nov 2000.
₹6,057 crore IPO; first insurer to list on NSE and BSE.
Sandeep Batra, ICICI Bank Executive Director, became Chairman.
Prudential agreed to buy 75% of Bharti Life and said it would cut its stake here to below 10%.
Renamed ICICI Life Insurance Ltd (22 Sep); ICICI Bank raised its stake to about 52.8%.
Sidharatha Mishra named MD & CEO from 14 Oct after Anup Bagchi left for HDFC Bank; new brand line 'Har Kal Aasaan' launched.

model.how: ICICI Life collects premiums from customers, through ICICI Bank and other bank partners, its own agents, brokers and online, and invests the money (₹3.29 lakh crore AUM) in bonds and shares. It pays death claims, maturity and survival benefits, and earns a profit over the life of each policy. Term (protection) and annuity plans earn higher margins, so it has been pushing them.
flow: Sells policies via banks, agents, partners and online
Invests in bonds and shares (AUM ₹3.29 lakh cr)
Pays claims and maturities; keeps the margin over many years

industry.regulator: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)
points: Bank-backed insurers depend on their parent bank's branches; IRDAI is consulting on distribution costs and commissions, which could change how much banks earn for selling policies.
Foreign partners are reshuffling: Prudential is moving to Bharti Life and cutting its stake here, so ICICI Bank now leads the company alone.
Big theme for interviews: growing high-margin term and annuity plans while customers often prefer market-linked ULIPs.

glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs and taxes. The company's final earnings.
glossary.Revenue: Total money earned from the business in a period, before costs.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year. Also called employee turnover.
glossary.IPO: Initial Public Offering: when a company first sells its shares to the public.
glossary.Market share: A company's sales as a % of the total sales of its industry.
glossary.Consolidated: Figures for the company together with its subsidiaries. 'Standalone' means the parent company alone.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer: checking a customer's identity before opening an account or selling a product.
glossary.IRDAI: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India: the regulator of all insurance companies.
glossary.Premium: The money a customer pays to buy an insurance policy.
glossary.Gross written premium: Total premium collected in a period, from new and renewing policies.
glossary.New business premium: Premium from policies sold for the first time in the period.
glossary.Renewal premium: Premium paid by existing customers to keep their policies going.
glossary.APE: Annualised Premium Equivalent: a standard measure of new sales. Regular premiums count fully, single premiums count 10%.
glossary.VNB: Value of New Business: the expected future profit (today's value) from policies sold in the period. A key measure for life insurers.
glossary.VNB margin: VNB as a % of APE. Shows how profitable new sales are.
glossary.Embedded value: The value of a life insurer today: its net worth plus the present value of future profits from existing policies.
glossary.Persistency: The % of customers who keep paying premiums after a set time (e.g. 13th month, 61st month). Higher is better.
glossary.Solvency ratio: Available capital compared with the capital the regulator requires. IRDAI's minimum is 150% (1.5 times).
glossary.AUM: Assets Under Management: the money the insurer invests on behalf of policyholders and shareholders.
glossary.Protection: Pure risk cover such as term insurance: pays only if something happens, cheap premium, high profit margin.
glossary.ULIP: Unit Linked Insurance Plan: part insurance, part market investment. Returns depend on markets.
glossary.Par / Non-par: Participating (par) policies share profits through bonuses; non-participating (non-par) policies give fixed, guaranteed benefits.
glossary.Annuity: A product that pays a regular income, usually after retirement, in return for a lump sum.
glossary.Bancassurance: Selling insurance through a bank's branches and customers. A main channel for bank-backed insurers.
glossary.Agency: Selling insurance through individual commission-based agents.
glossary.Surrender: When a customer exits a policy early and gets back part of the money.
glossary.Claim settlement ratio: The % of claims an insurer pays out of those it receives. Higher means more claims paid.
glossary.GST on insurance: Tax charged on premiums. From 22 Sep 2025 the government removed GST on individual life and health policies.
glossary.Bima Sugam: An IRDAI online marketplace planned to let customers buy, compare and service insurance in one place.
glossary.Promoter: The main owner group that controls a listed company. ICICI Bank is the promoter here; Prudential is now treated as an ordinary investor.
glossary.Joint venture: A company set up and owned by two partners, like ICICI Bank and Prudential plc in 2000.
glossary.Rebranding: Changing a company's name, logo or tagline. ICICI Prudential Life became ICICI Life Insurance in Sep 2026, with the line 'Har Kal Aasaan'.
glossary.Offer for sale: When existing shareholders sell their shares to the public; the company itself gets no money.
glossary.Sum assured: The amount the insurer promises to pay if the insured person dies during the policy.
glossary.Cost to premium ratio: Operating costs and commissions as a % of premium. Lower means more efficient.

Role knowledge, the company and HR questions

Finance.q: What is VNB margin, and what was ICICI Life's recently?
Finance.a: VNB margin is the value of new business as a % of APE: how profitable new sales are. It was 24.7% in FY26 and 26.0% in H1 FY27, helped by more term (protection) sales.

Finance.q: Why did the company's VNB margin rise?
Finance.a: Product mix: protection and annuity plans, which earn higher margins, grew faster than savings plans. Protection APE rose about 40% in H1 FY27.

Finance.q: What does a solvency ratio of 229.9% mean?
Finance.a: The insurer holds about 2.3 times the capital IRDAI requires; the minimum is 150%. It shows the company can pay claims even in bad times.

Marketing.q: Why did ICICI Prudential Life change its name, and how would you communicate it?
Marketing.a: Prudential is cutting its stake below 10%, so ICICI Bank leads alone. Tell customers that policies, benefits and claims are unchanged, and use the trusted ICICI name with the new 'Har Kal Aasaan' line.

Marketing.q: How would you sell term insurance to a 25-year-old?
Marketing.a: Make it simple: low premium at a young age, big cover for the family, and fast claims (99.3% settled). Use digital journeys and ICICI Bank's app.

HR.q: How would you reduce early attrition among insurance advisors?
HR.a: Better onboarding and training, mentors, digital selling tools, quick first commissions and recognition for good performers.

Sales.a: Ask about retirement goals, show how a small monthly amount grows over time, explain guaranteed income from an annuity, and offer to review the plan every year.

Operations.q: How can technology improve claims and policy issue?
Operations.a: Online KYC, auto underwriting and digital documents. ICICI Life says it issues about 54% of savings policies the same day and settles claims in about a day on average.

Other.q: What does Prudential's stake cut mean for the company?
Other.a: Prudential will sell down from about 22% to below 10% after buying Bharti Life. ICICI Bank has raised its stake to about 52.8% and remains the promoter, so control stays with ICICI.

interview.why_us: ICICI Life was India's first listed insurer and protects over 7 crore lives. It is in an exciting phase: a new name and brand, a new CEO from ICICI Bank's digital side, and fast growth in term insurance, with VNB margin up to 26%. Working here means learning insurance with the strength of the ICICI group behind me. I want to contribute to [your role] as it grows.
ask: How will the move to an ICICI-only brand change the way the company sells and serves customers?
Which channel, bank, agency or digital, do you see growing fastest in the next two years?
What does success look like for a new joiner in the first six months?

gd.t: Should bank-owned insurers be allowed to sell mainly their parent's products in bank branches?
gd.for: Customers trust their bank, and it brings insurance to many people cheaply.
gd.against: Risk of mis-selling and less choice for customers; IRDAI is reviewing commissions.

gd.t: Is term insurance better than savings-linked insurance for young Indians?
gd.for: Term gives large cover cheaply; savings can go into mutual funds or PPF.
gd.against: Many people want guaranteed returns and forced savings that endowment plans give.

avoid: Don't call it 'ICICI Prudential Life' as if nothing changed; it was renamed ICICI Life Insurance Ltd on 22 Sep 2026.
Don't name Anup Bagchi as CEO; he left in Oct 2026 to head HDFC Bank. Sidharatha Mishra leads now.
Don't mix up the life insurer with ICICI Prudential AMC (mutual funds, listed Dec 2025) or ICICI Lombard (general insurance).
